title: Janos Papai (Constantinople) to Ferenc Rakoczi II, 1706-1710, in the envoy key R580 (DECODE R740, R741, R757, R765, R784, R793-R796, R805, R823)

steps.what: Fetched the DECODE records, transcriptions and the R740 images with the project cookie.
Searched DECODE key records for NAH keys tagged Constantinople; R580 is headed 'key given to Janos Papai' (copies R581, R452).
Applied R581's table to R805: 336/336 groups give continuous Hungarian.
Applied the same table to R823, R765, R757, R741: 97.7-99.5% of groups in key.
Transcribed the numeric passage of R740 from the image (168 groups) and read it in full.
Web search for a printed decipherment: Benda 1963 edition of Papai's Turkish diaries exists, contents not checked.
Catalogue target 'Unknown sender to Rakoczi II, 1707' (DECODE R784): fetched record, transcription and both images.
Scored every NAH key record on DECODE (97 transcriptions) against R784; the Constantinople key R581 (Papai's) gave running Hungarian.
Read R784 with decode.py unchanged: 587/594 groups in key; French ambassador's report on the Porte and war.
Catalogue 47 'Constantinople envoys to Rakoczi II' (DECODE R793-R796): fetched four records and transcriptions; four despatches, not two.
Applied Papai's key R581 (decode.py) unchanged: R793/R794/R796 97.4-98.0% in key; R794 and R795 signed/dated Constantinople 1706.
R795 only 83.9% in key: 251 groups 323-740. Compared with the contemporary interlinear: the decipherer skips them, so nulls.
decode_nulls.py: 5,012 of 5,043 groups read (4,706 table values + 306 nulls), 31 slips.
Benda (ed.) 1963 edition of Papai's Turkish diaries: not online, antiquarian copies only.
decode2.py: split run-together groups, re-join split groups, 3-digit >322 as nulls (R823 clear numerals), 220 = a from context.
Second pass over the eleven numeric letters: 16,641 of 16,698 groups read (99.66%).
Rescored every remaining off-key group with the 4-gram model in context (retry_groups.py): no clear winner for the 57 left.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from papai1706, which had joined Papai's eleven numeric letters in the envoy key R580/R581 with R731 (6 Mar 1710), whose passages are in a separate graphic-sign alphabet. This profile keeps the eleven numeric letters (R580 key) only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): DECODE transcriptions DOC_<record>_*.txt (R740 transcribed here), second-pass readings <record>_read2.txt with the first-pass DOC_<record>_read.txt (R740: R740_read.txt); key R581/R580 transcriptions

outcome.method_basis: DECODE key R580/R581, headed 'key given to János Pápai', from the same Rákóczi archive (MNL OL G15), was applied to DECODE's transcriptions of the eleven numeric letters and read 99.7% of groups.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode2.py over the DECODE transcriptions of the eleven numeric letters: 16,641 of 16,698 numeric groups (nulls counted read); the ~41 tokens DECODE marks '?' added as unread: 16,641/~16,739. Before the split R731's ~330 signs were also counted unread (0.97).
outcome.notes: Eleven numeric letters read at 99.7% of groups after the second pass; 57 scattered groups (DECODE digit slips) and ~41 '?' tokens open, all blocked by the transcription. Split 14 Oct 2026: R731's graphic-sign passages are papai1710; on the eleven letters alone the read bar is met, so the class is read (was read in part).

texts.label: R805, 1 May 1706, Constantinople
texts.summary: The envoys urge that the Porte refuse the Imperial troops free passage across Ottoman ground, and that the border pashas, the Pasha of Arad among them, not allow the Germans passage towards Szeged without orders; they have spoken to the Vezír about their affairs and about Muscovy.

texts.label: R795, 1 Jan 1706, Constantinople
texts.summary: Pápai with Ferenc Horváth reports the Prince's discretion money handed to the Vezír's Kiaya, the Tatar Khan, the French ambassador, the Pasha of Temesvár, a Croatian incursion, and letters to go via Moldavia so that the Prince's news arrives faster.

texts.label: R796, 20 Feb 1706, Constantinople
texts.summary: The Prince's undated letter from the Tisza received; the Germans spread false news; the confederates are scorned; the Moldavian kapi-kiaya as channel; the Muscovite envoy, the Vezír and the Sultan; nothing resolved on the propositions.

texts.label: R793, March 1706, Constantinople
texts.summary: Secret talks with the Porte's chancellor about the Muscovite-Porte quarrel, the King of Sweden, a Hungarian confederation with the Porte on certain conditions, the Circassians and the Black Sea; the Prince's manifesto translated and given to the Vezír.

texts.label: R794, undated, early 1706
texts.summary: Propositions on recruiting four thousand horse in Wallachia, the memorial on Muscovy, and the (French) King's money that the ambassador will not pay without the King's order.

texts.label: R823, 19 Dec 1706, Constantinople
texts.summary: Report of an audience at the Porte in the presence of the Imperial internuncio, partly in Latin, with the argument over hereditary kingship and the envoys' reply that Hungary cannot give up its old laws.

texts.label: R765, 5 Jan 1707
texts.summary: Submission to the Prince's will, the Polish situation, and approaches to the French ambassador on the Prince's orders.

texts.label: R784, undated [1707], unsigned
texts.summary: The French ambassador reported that no arguments could bring the Porte to war, though the grandees and the whole Turkish nation incline to it; France means to turn Turkey wholly against the Germans, which would harm Hungary; if Muscovy and Poland do not second it, the Germans will overrun Hungary. A note in another hand asks the Prince to keep it secret and decipher it himself.

texts.label: R757, 16 May 1708
texts.summary: The Muscovite ambassador's message; the envoy cannot send money from Constantinople; Hentér.

texts.label: R740, 2 Jan 1710, Constantinople
texts.summary: The Kiaya's answer, in cipher: be patient, do not hurry, wait; if the Porte does not take the matter to heart, Rákóczi should not spend money and effort at the Porte in vain.

texts.label: R741, 8 May 1710, Constantinople
texts.summary: At the Defterdar's; the Pasha of Belgrade's letter concerned only the merchants' affairs.

prior.where: DECODE marked R805 partly decrypted (interlinear syllables); Benda's 1963 edition of Papai's Turkish diaries not checked
